formation.title: The Crown of Bohemia
formation.text:
The lands of Bohemia and Moravia are united under a single crown. For generations, this kingdom has stood at the crossroads of European civilization, seat of emperors, cradle of religious revolt, and home to one of the oldest universities north of the Alps.

But Bohemia's identity remains contested. The memory of Jan Hus and the Hussite wars lingers in every parish and estate chamber. The chalice and the crown pull in opposite directions: shall Bohemia be defined by the radical legacy of its religious dissenters, with their democratic assemblies and military innovations? Or by the ancient prestige of Saint Wenceslas's crown, with its imperial connections, cultural patronage, and place among the great Catholic kingdoms of Europe?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: The Chalice shall not be silenced.

modifiers.name: Hussite Heritage
modifiers.text: The chalice of Hus burns in the hearts of the Bohemian people. Religious dissent, military innovation, and the power of the estates define this kingdom.

options.text: We wear the Crown of Saint Wenceslas.

modifiers.name: Crown of Saint Wenceslas
modifiers.text: The sacred crown of Bohemia bestows imperial prestige and cultural patronage upon its wearer. Prague shines as a jewel of Christendom.

advances.name: Silver Legacy of Kutna Hora
advances.text: The rich silver deposits of Kutna Hora made Bohemia one of the wealthiest kingdoms in medieval Europe, producing a third of all European silver.

advances.name: Premyslid Crown Governance
advances.text: The Premyslid dynasty established the administrative foundations of the Bohemian crown, centralizing royal authority over the Czech lands.

advances.name: Bohemian Hop Cultivation
advances.text: Bohemia's Saaz hops were so prized that exporting hop sprouts was punishable by death. The brewing tradition dates to the earliest monasteries.

advances.name: Charles University
advances.text: Founded in 1348 by Charles IV, the University of Prague was the first university in Central Europe and attracted scholars from across the continent.

advances.name: Prague's Golden Age
advances.text: Under Charles IV, Prague became a center of Gothic art and architecture. The Charles Bridge, St. Vitus Cathedral, and the New Town transformed the city.

advances.name: Houfnice Field Guns
advances.text: The Czech houfnice, mobile field cannon, gave the English language the word 'howitzer.' Hussite gunners pioneered the use of artillery in open battle.

advances.name: Tabor Warfare
advances.text: The radical Hussites built the fortified town of Tabor as a model community and military base. Their defensive tactics combined wagenburg, firearms, and faith.

advances.name: Compactata of Basel
advances.text: The 1436 agreement between the Council of Basel and the Hussites was the first negotiated religious settlement in European history.

event.title: The Compactata of Basel
event.text:
After decades of devastating religious warfare, an extraordinary agreement has been reached. The Council of Basel has recognized the rights of the Utraquist Church in Bohemia, the first time in Christian history that a dissident religious movement has wrested formal concessions from the Roman Church.

The Compacts of Basel guarantee communion in both kinds, allow lay preaching, and acknowledge the expropriation of Church lands. Bohemia stands as a unique experiment in religious coexistence, a century before the Reformation will convulse the rest of Europe. The moderate Hussites have secured what the radicals fought and died for at Lipany, not through victory in battle, but through the exhaustion of their enemies and the pragmatism of their diplomats.

options.text: Sub utraque specie, under both kinds.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Compactata
modifiers.text: The Basel Compacts secured Bohemia's right to communion in both kinds. Religious coexistence, however uneasy, prevails in the Czech lands.

advances.name: Hussite Peasant Levies
advances.text: The Hussite wars mobilized Bohemian peasants as never before. Armed with war flails, halberds, and righteous fury, they defeated crusading knights.

advances.name: Unity of the Brethren
advances.text: The Bohemian Brethren, heirs to the Hussite tradition, emphasized education, literacy, and moral discipline. Jan Amos Comenius became the father of modern pedagogy.

advances.name: Bohemian Professional Infantry
advances.text: Building on Hussite military tradition, Bohemia developed disciplined professional infantry skilled in pike and shot warfare.

advances.name: Bohemian Estate Diets
advances.text: The Bohemian Diet was one of the most powerful representative assemblies in Europe, with the right to elect kings and approve taxation.

advances.name: Verneuerte Landesordnung
advances.text: Ferdinand II's Renewed Land Ordinance of 1627 swept away the old Bohemian constitution, imposing absolute Habsburg rule after the Battle of White Mountain.

event.title: The Renewed Land Ordinance
event.text:
The catastrophe at White Mountain has transformed Bohemia. The Protestant estates who dared to elect Frederick of the Palatinate as their king have been crushed, their leaders executed on the Old Town Square, their properties confiscated. Ferdinand II's Renewed Land Ordinance of 1627 has swept away the old Bohemian constitution, the Estates Diet that once elected kings is now a rubber stamp, the Czech language is demoted to equality with German, and only the Catholic faith is permitted.

But this devastation also presents a choice. The old Bohemia of competing confessions is dead. What rises from these ashes will be shaped by how its rulers wield this absolute power.

options.text: Enforce the true faith without compromise.

modifiers.name: Counter-Reformation
modifiers.text: The Renewed Land Ordinance has imposed Catholic conformity upon Bohemia. The old Hussite liberties are extinguished, but order is restored.

options.text: Let the exiles carry our learning to the world.

modifiers.name: Legacy of the Exiles
modifiers.text: The Bohemian Brethren carry their learning into exile, spreading Czech scholarship across Europe. What was lost in faith endures in thought.

advances.name: Recatholicization
advances.text: The forced re-Catholicization of Bohemia after 1620 expelled Protestant clergy, confiscated estates, and imposed religious conformity across the kingdom.

advances.name: Baroque Prague
advances.text: The counter-reformation transformed Prague's skyline with spectacular Baroque churches, palaces, and gardens built by Italian and Austrian architects.

advances.name: Bohemian Glass Trade
advances.text: Bohemian crystal glass became a luxury export across Europe in the 17th and 18th centuries, rivaling Venetian murano as the continent's finest.

advances.name: Czech National Awakening
advances.text: Scholars and writers rediscovered the Czech language and Hussite heritage, forging a modern national identity from the fragments of a suppressed culture.

event.title: The Czech National Awakening
event.text:
Something stirs in the libraries and lecture halls of Prague. Scholars like Josef Dobrovsky and Josef Jungmann are reconstructing the Czech language from the fragments left after two centuries of Germanization. They rediscover the Hussite legacy not as heresy but as national heritage, proof that the Czech people once defied all of Europe and won.

The National Awakening is more than a linguistic movement. It is a reassertion of Bohemian identity, connecting the medieval kingdom of Charles IV through the Hussite revolution to the modern demand for national self-determination. Czech culture, long suppressed, now demands its place in the sun.

advances.name: Industrial Bohemia
advances.text: Bohemia became one of the most industrialized regions of Central Europe, with iron foundries, textile mills, and a dense railway network.

advances.name: The Pilsner Revolution
advances.text:
In 1842, the Pilsen Burgher Brewery produced the first golden lager using Saaz hops and soft Pilsen water, creating a beer style that conquered the world.

Available in: Bohemian Brewhouse

advances.name: Constitutional Struggle
advances.text: The demand for Bohemian autonomy within the Habsburg monarchy drove constitutional debates and the emergence of modern Czech political life.

destiny.name: Destiny of Bohemia
destiny.text: The crown lands are united. Now Bohemia must choose its path, the chalice of Hus or the crown of Wenceslas, and pursue its destiny to completion.

event.title: The Destiny of Bohemia
event.text: The Bohemian crown lands are consolidated under a single ruler. The kingdom stands at a crossroads. Shall the legacy of Hus guide its armies outward in holy war, or shall the memory of Charles IV draw scholars and artisans to Prague, making it the jewel of an empire? The path chosen now will shape the destiny of the Czech people for centuries to come.

destiny.name: The Beautiful Rides
destiny.text: The Hussite war bands launched devastating raids, the spanile jizdy, deep into Saxony, Brandenburg, and Silesia, spreading terror and the word of God. Seize Wroclaw and Zittau to secure Bohemia's eastern and northern flanks.

event.title: The Beautiful Rides Begin
event.text: The Hussite field armies have broken through the mountain passes and seized the great cities beyond. Wroclaw, capital of Silesia, and Zittau, the richest town of the Lusatian League, now fly the chalice banner. The spanile jizdy, the Beautiful Rides that once terrorized half of Europe, have become permanent conquests. The crusaders who once marched against Bohemia now cower behind their walls as the warriors of God ride forth.

options.text: God wills it, in both kinds.

destiny.name: Bohemian Hegemony
destiny.text: With Silesia and Lusatia secured, the Hussite armies can push into the heart of Saxony. Dresden and Meissen are to be taken, and half of Upper Saxony held, as far as the rides once reached.

conditions.text: At least 50% of the locations of Upper Saxony are ours

event.title: The Hegemony of the Chalice
event.text: Saxon resistance has crumbled. Dresden and Meissen, the heartland of the Wettin dynasty, are now subject to Bohemian arms. The Hussite military machine, forged in decades of defensive war, has become the dominant force in Central Europe. But hegemony demands choices. Shall Bohemia's strength rest on the iron flail of its warriors, or on the fiery sermons of its field preachers who sustain the army's fanatical morale?

options.text: Let the flail do the preaching.

modifiers.name: Iron Flail
modifiers.text: The Hussite war flail crushes all resistance. Walls are stormed and every victory hardens the field armies, though the devastation of war stunts the growth of the common folk.

options.text: The word of God sustains our armies.

modifiers.name: Field Preachers
modifiers.text: Hussite preachers march with the armies, restoring their spirit after every fight and drawing volunteers from every village. The cost of this zealous mobilization weighs on the treasury.

destiny.name: Warriors of God
destiny.text: The Hussite revolution reaches its apex. Nuremberg, Berlin, and Krakow must fall, and half of Franconia be held, to prove that no crusade can break the warriors of God. This is the capstone of Bohemian military supremacy.

conditions.text: At least 50% of the locations of Franconia are ours

event.title: Warriors of God
event.text:
Nuremberg, Berlin, Krakow, the great cities of Central Europe have fallen to Bohemian arms. No crusade, no coalition, no emperor could stop the advance of the warriors of God. What the Hussites began as a desperate defense of their communion chalice has become the most remarkable military expansion in European history. Jan Zizka's blind genius has found its ultimate expression.

But every empire must decide how to govern its conquests. Shall Bohemia rule through military discipline alone, or attempt the radical experiment of extending its proto-democratic assemblies to the conquered lands?

options.text: Discipline and the sword shall govern.

modifiers.name: Warriors of God
modifiers.text: The disciplined armies of the Hussite state march with divine purpose, their supply lines efficient and their enemies withering in hostile Bohemian territory.

options.text: Let every land have its assembly.

modifiers.name: Hussite Commonwealth
modifiers.text: The radical Hussite vision of community governance extends across conquered lands, binding them to the kingdom and raising popular armies quickly, though the decentralized treasury increases borrowing costs.

destiny.name: The Carolinum
destiny.text: Charles IV founded the first university north of the Alps and made Prague a center of European learning. Give the university a library in Prague and build the treasury to fund Bohemia's cultural ambitions.

conditions.text: We own Prague and it has a Library

event.title: The New Carolinum
event.text: Prague's scholarly tradition, founded by Charles IV himself, has produced a new generation of thinkers and administrators. Its new library draws scholars to Prague, and a full royal treasury attracts merchants from across Europe. The Carolinum, once merely a university, has become the intellectual engine of a kingdom that leads by knowledge rather than conquest.

options.text: Prague shall be the Athens of the North.

destiny.name: Imperial Capital
destiny.text: Prague was once the seat of the Holy Roman Emperor. Secure Vienna, build up Kutna Hora, whose silver pays for the court, and restore Bohemia's position as the premier kingdom of Central Europe.

conditions.text: We own Kutna Hora and its development is at least 32

event.title: The Imperial Capital Restored
event.text:
Vienna is secured and the realm thrives. Bohemia has reclaimed the imperial stature it held under Charles IV, when Prague was the undisputed capital of the Holy Roman Empire. The kingdom's institutional sophistication and cultural prestige draw ambassadors and scholars from across the continent.

But imperial ambition comes in different forms. Shall Bohemia invoke the Golden Bull of 1356, Charles IV's constitutional masterwork, to cement its diplomatic supremacy? Or invest in Prague's workshops and artisans to build an economic foundation that no rival can match?

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Golden Bull
modifiers.text: The constitutional framework of the Golden Bull elevates Bohemia's diplomatic standing among the princes of Europe, though maintaining this prestige demands a costlier court.

modifiers.name: Prague Workshops
modifiers.text: Prague's artisans and builders produce works of exceptional quality at lower cost, though the kingdom's focus on crafts leaves fewer men to refill the ranks.

destiny.name: Praga Caput Regni
destiny.text: Prague, Head of the Kingdom, and perhaps of all Europe. Control Augsburg, found an Arts Academy in Prague as Rudolf II gathered artists and astronomers at his court, and build Prague up into a capital without equal in culture and learning.

conditions.text: We own Prague and it has an Arts Academy
We own Prague and its development is at least 72

event.title: Praga Caput Regni
event.text:
Prague, Head of the Kingdom. The ancient motto has never been more true. With Augsburg secured and the Arts Academy drawing painters and astronomers to the court, Prague stands as the cultural and institutional capital of Central Europe, a role it has not held since the golden days of Charles IV. The dream of a Bohemian-led empire, built on scholarship rather than conquest, is now reality.

Shall Bohemia claim the ultimate prize, the title Rex Romanorum, King of the Romans, and rule Europe through prestige and precedence? Or turn inward, fostering a Bohemian enlightenment that will illuminate the world through knowledge?

modifiers.name: Rex Romanorum
modifiers.text: Bohemia's king claims the ancient title of King of the Romans. Imperial prestige is unassailable, though the burdens of maintaining this status weary the realm in wartime.

modifiers.name: Bohemian Enlightenment
modifiers.text: Prague leads a scholarly revolution that reaches the villages: schools are opened in every parish, and the learned trades of the towns are opened to their pupils.

units.name: Houfnice
units.text: Mobile Hussite field guns, the precursor to the modern howitzer. Light enough to keep pace with the wagenburg, devastating enough to break cavalry charges.

units.name: Cepnik
units.text: Hussite peasant warriors armed with war flails, the cep. Fanatical in defense, they broke the flower of European chivalry at Vitkov and Kutna Hora.

units.name: Bohemian Landsknecht
units.text: Professional Bohemian pikemen and halberdiers, heirs to the Hussite infantry tradition. Disciplined formations trained to hold against cavalry.

buildings.name: Kutna Hora Mint
buildings.text: The Italian Court at Kutna Hora minted the Prague Groschen and later the Thaler for over four centuries, making Bohemia's coinage the standard of Central Europe.

buildings.name: Bohemian Brewhouse
buildings.text: A licensed brewery using the prized Saaz hops of Bohemia. Royal brewing privileges ensure quality and restrict competition.

buildings.name: Hussite Tabor
buildings.text: A fortified settlement in the Hussite tradition, part garrison, part community, designed for sustained defense with firearms and wagons.

buildings.name: Karolinum
buildings.text: A university in the tradition of Charles IV's foundation at Prague, the first university in Central Europe, center of theology, law, and the liberal arts.

buildings.name: Baroque Church
buildings.text: A magnificent counter-reformation church built in the ornate Baroque style, a monument to Catholic resurgence and Habsburg cultural patronage in Bohemia.

buildings.name: Bohemian Ironworks
buildings.text: A modern iron smelting works using Bohemia's rich deposits of iron and coal to produce high-quality steel for industry and export.

buildings.name: Hussite Arsenal
buildings.text: A great armory and workshop complex in the Hussite tradition, producing war wagons, field guns, and the feared flail weapons of the Bohemian infantry.

buildings.name: Imperial Academy
buildings.text: A supreme institution of learning in the tradition of Charles IV, rivaling Bologna and Paris as a center of European scholarship and institutional innovation.

list.name: Zemský sněm
list.text: The Land Diet of Bohemia summoned three estates (the panstvo, lords including the bishops; the rytířstvo, knights; and the deputies of the royal cities) to Prague or Kutná Hora to vote taxes, elect kings, and audit the Crown's affairs. Peasants had no representation. The Vladislav Land Ordinance of 1500 codified the Diet's powers and is regarded as the oldest written Czech constitution; the Bohemian Confederation of 1619 pushed those powers to their breaking point. The Diet's chairman was the Supreme Burgrave, presiding from his seat in Prague Castle.

list.name: Desky zemské
list.text: The Land Tables, established under Přemysl Otakar II in the thirteenth century, were the registry of allodial estates, Diet resolutions, and Land Court rulings of the Bohemian crown. Property transfers between nobles were valid only when entered in the books, which gave the szlachta of Bohemia a written-law guarantee against arbitrary seizure two centuries before such guarantees became common elsewhere. The Tables remained the operative cadastre of the kingdom until 1848, with parallel registers for Moravia and Silesia.

list.name: Zemský soud
list.text: The Land Court of Bohemia, the supreme judicial body for the noble estates, sat in Prague Castle under the presidency of the Supreme Burgrave with the great barons of the realm as assessors. Its judgments were entered in the Land Tables and considered final; the Lesser Land Court (Menší zemský soud) handled cases below the noble threshold. Royal will was tempered by a court the king did not fully control, and the gentry's collective memory of its judgments shaped what they would and would not accept from a new king at his coronation oath.

list.name: Nejvyšší purkrabství pražské
list.text: The Supreme Burgrave of Prague Castle was the kingdom's highest land officer and the king's deputy in his absence, holding judicial, military, and administrative authority over the realm. From the fourteenth century the Burgrave presided over the Land Court and signed for the Crown when the monarch was abroad: the natural channel for an itinerant Luxembourg or absentee Habsburg ruler. The Burgrave's house, originally Gothic and rebuilt many times, still stands within the walls of Prague Castle. The office was abolished only in 1848.

list.name: Kompaktáta
list.text: The Compacts of Basel, negotiated with the Council of Basel and ratified by the Bohemian estates at Jihlava on 5 July 1436, ended the Hussite wars by granting the Utraquists their four demands: communion in both kinds (sub utraque specie, bread and wine for the laity), free preaching of God's word, the punishment of public sins by the proper authority, and the expropriation of Roman Church lands seized during the wars. An independent Bohemian Catholic church under an elected archbishop was tolerated. Pope Eugene IV refused to ratify the document, but for nearly a century it was the operative law of religious coexistence in the Czech crown lands: a confessional patchwork enacted a hundred years before the Peace of Augsburg.

list.name: Kutnohorský dekret
list.text: On 18 January 1409, Wenceslaus IV signed the Decree of Kutná Hora, reweighting the votes of the four faculty nations of the Charles University in Prague: three votes to the Bohemian nation, one to the Bavarian, Saxon, and Polish nations combined. About eighty percent of the German masters and their students walked out, founding what became the University of Leipzig. The Hus circle gained the chairs they needed; Czech became a working academic language; and Prague's cosmopolitan studium contracted into a national one. Some historians read the decree as the first Czech nationalist document.

list.name: Obnovené zřízení zemské
list.text: The Renewed Land Ordinance, promulgated by Ferdinand II on 10 May 1627 in the wake of White Mountain, dismantled the constitutional achievements of three centuries. The Bohemian crown was declared a hereditary Habsburg possession, the elective monarchy abolished, Catholicism alone permitted, and German placed on equal footing with Czech in administration. The Diet survived only as a registry for royal decrees; the Compactata were torn up; the great Protestant nobility had been executed at the Old Town Square in 1621, exiled, or expropriated. The Czech kingdom became, in all but name, a province of the Habsburg state.
